newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian radio investment blocked - DMG Radio.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian radio investment blocked - DMG Radio.

text.p: Hundreds of millions of dollars of investment funds are stagnating or being redirected because of delays in releasing new FM radio licences throughout Australia, a senior industry figure said on Wednesday.

Paul Thompson, chief executive of the British-owned DMG Radio Australia which is trying to build a network in Australia, said the profitability of the major groups in capital city radio was infinitely higher than ever before.
DMG Radio, owned by Daily Mail & General Trust Plc, has 15 licences for Australian radio stations in mostly regional centres.

"Now here is nothing wrong with high profits but this profitability is made possible and institutionalised by the radio frequency planning process which places new capital city FM licences on almost perpetual delay," he told a media lunch.
Thompson said the Broadcasting Services Act of 1992 proposed the granting of new capital city FM licences by auction in 1995 but it was now possible none would be granted this decade.

"And while we wait, the incumbents' profits grow exponentially, hundreds of million of dollars of investment funds stagnate or are re-directed, radio station licences surge to unprecedented, unrealistic and unsustainable levels and
listeners simply miss out," he said.
He said the forthcoming results of the Federal government's cross media ownership review was likely to see newspaper and television groups able to buy radio stations and groups.

"So in a market where there is an enormous number of buyers and almost no sellers and no new capital city licences, the government will do nothing to ease the chronic shortage of supply of licences but will accentuate the already massive demand by creating new buyers," he said.
He said if radio was to meet the challenges of the computer age, it must have a regulatory structure administered with sufficient efficiency.
